correctness.rationale: A direct Wang-sequence reconstruction uses the matrix \(A=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\) on \(H^2(S^2\times S^2;\mathbb Z)\), with Smith invariants \((1,2)\) for \(A-I\), and degree-four monodromy \(-1\). Since the fiber has vanishing odd cohomology, \(H^2(N;\mathbb Z)=H^4(N;\mathbb Z)=0\) and \(H^3(N;\mathbb Z)=H^5(N;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z/2\). The unique nonzero mod-two invariant \(\xi\) restricts to \(\bar u+\bar v\). Its Pontryagin square restricts to \(2uv\) in \(H^4(S^2\times S^2;\mathbb Z/4)\), generating the image of the injective restriction from \(H^4(N;\mathbb Z/4)\). The coefficient Bockstein \(\beta_4\) is injective because \(H^4(N;\mathbb Z)=0\), so \(\widetilde Q(\beta_2\xi)\) has order two, with no quotient indeterminacy. Antieau--Williams Theorem A gives \(\operatorname{ind}(\beta_2\xi)=4\), and Becerra--Lupercio Theorem 7.5 realizes actual minimum regular rank eight. Integral Poincaré duality gives the general upper bound; a published rank-four three-dimensional gerbe times \(S^2\) and trivial gerbes realize the other minima. A finite exact-arithmetic checker passes; it does not replace the general cohomology and bundle existence theorems.
